entry.title: When two children want to play together
entry.summary: Davies describes an interest in playing together that may emerge around 2½. Watch whether both children welcome it, and help when one wants to return to playing alone.
entry.cue: One child approaches another’s activity, or a short shared game begins.
detail: Before about 2½, Davies describes toddlers as mainly playing alongside each other. She notes that children with siblings or regular peer company may share earlier. These are broad observations, rather than a timetable for a particular child.

Even when children want to play together, they may need help finding words or noticing that the other child has finished sharing the moment. Davies describes acknowledging that one child wants to play alone and returning for a turn later.

Her turn-taking approach supports the child already using an activity and the child waiting. The adult still steps in to stop pushing or grabbing. In a shared public place, she allows a shorter ending so someone else can have a turn.

ageContext.bookAge: Before 2.5 years mainly parallel play; around 2.5 years possible shared play, sometimes earlier with siblings or regular peer contact.
ageContext.readiness: Observe whether both children welcome watching or joining, and when one wants to play alone.
ageContext.note: The book describes a possible change around 2½, not an expectation throughout this age band.
